content.title: About
content.content: Bacalaitos fritos are fried cod fish pieces, popular in Latin American cuisine, especially in Portugal and the Caribbean. The cod is cut into bite‑size chunks, coated in a batter of flour, eggs and spices, then deep‑fried until golden and crisp. The result is a crunchy, lightly salty snack often served with chili or lime sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Spanish word “bacalao,” meaning cod.
Traditionally they are made from dried, salted cod, but many modern recipes use fresh fish.
In Portugal they are commonly served as tapas together with marinated olives and bread.
In some Caribbean islands they are paired with mango or pineapple salsa.
The batter often includes paprika, garlic and oregano, giving the dish its characteristic aroma.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Cod provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many fried snacks, bacalaitos contain relatively modest amounts of saturated fat when cooked in moderate oil.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 in cod supports nervous system function and blood formation.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium contributes to immune health and has antioxidant properties.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Cod provides modest amounts of omega‑3s, beneficial for heart and vascular health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including cod.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Traditional recipes use salted cod, which can make the final product high in sodium.

items.title: Frying oil
items.content: Excessive frying adds calories and may produce trans‑fatty acids.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Commercial versions may contain preservatives and flavor enhancers that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve bacalaitos hot as an appetizer, accompanied by chili sauce, lime aioli, garlic mayo, or simply a squeeze of lemon. They can also be added to salads, tacos, or used as a filling for sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked bacalaitos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag – they retain flavor and texture for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven to restore crispness.

cookie-chocolate-with-icing-or-coating.title: Cookie, chocolate, with icing or coating

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate cookie with icing or coating is a small baked treat made from flour, sugar, butter and cocoa, covered with a sweet chocolate glaze or coating. It features a crisp outer edge, a soft interior, and a rich chocolate flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chocolate cookies appeared in Europe in the 19th century as a cocoa‑enhanced version of traditional biscuits.
The glaze can be dark or milk chocolate, sometimes enriched with nuts or dried fruit.
Cookies are often used as a base for desserts such as tiramisu or truffles.
In many countries chocolate cookies are served with tea or coffee as a sweet accompaniment.
There are countless recipe variations, including gluten‑free and vegan versions.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in chocolate is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Mood support
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, contributing to a better mood.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat provides a quick source of energy.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Chocolate cookies contain magnesium, iron and zinc, important for metabolic processes.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour, the cookies can supply dietary fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional cookies contain wheat, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Nut and dairy allergies
items.content: The icing often contains milk and nuts, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chocolate coating adds significant calories, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cookies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with tea or coffee, used in layered desserts, crumbled over ice cream, or used as a coating for fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator to prevent the glaze from melting. Avoid exposure to direct sunlight.

content.title: About
content.content: A peanut butter and jelly sandwich consists of two slices of white bread spread with regular peanut butter and regular fruit jelly. It is a classic American snack loved for its sweet‑salty flavor combination.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded peanut butter and jelly sandwich dates back to 1901 in the United States.
In the 1940s the sandwich became a staple in American school lunch programs.
There are many variations: different breads, nut butters (almond, cashew) and jams (strawberry, raspberry, grape).
In 2019 more than 2.5 billion peanut butter‑jelly sandwiches were sold in the U.S.
In Japan a popular version replaces jelly with a sweet soy glaze.

items.title: Source of protein and healthy fats
items.content: Peanut butter provides plant‑based protein and monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Peanut butter contains niacin, thiamine and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from the jelly
items.content: Fruit jelly supplies vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The sandwich rapidly replenishes glucose stores, making it a good pre‑exercise snack.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: White bread provides simple carbohydrates and a small amount of fiber for easy digestion.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanut butter can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Jelly often contains added sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Some brands of jelly and bread contain salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is typically eaten at room temperature. Cut it in half or quarters for easy handling. For a healthier twist, use whole‑grain bread instead of white.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Keep opened peanut butter and jelly refrigerated to prevent mold growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Apple pie is a classic dessert made from a pastry crust filled with sliced apples, sugar, cinnamon, and sometimes raisins. The crust can be flaky, shortcrust, or yeasted, while the filling is typically soft, aromatic, and mildly sweet‑tart.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Apple pie is considered a national dish in the United States, with a National Apple Pie Day celebrated on May 23.
Traditional recipes often blend several apple varieties to achieve a balance of sweetness and acidity.
The classic American serving includes a scoop of vanilla ice cream, known as "à la mode."
In medieval times, apple pies were open‑topped tarts; the covered version became popular in England later.
There are countless variations: with nuts, caramel, cream, or even cheese.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Apples provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestion and promoting satiety.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Apple skins are high in polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Apples contain vitamin C, vitamin K, potassium, and small amounts of B‑vitamins.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Fiber and flavonoids can help lower cholesterol and improve blood vessel function.

items.title: Moderate natural sugar
items.content: The natural sweetness of apples allows for reduced added sugar compared with many desserts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: When a lot of sugar is added, the pie can become calorie‑dense and unsuitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to apples or experience cross‑reaction with birch pollen.

items.title: Trans fats in crust
items.content: Using margarine or butter high in trans fats can worsen the fat profile of the pastry.

items.title: Overeating
items.content: Large portions may lead to excess calorie intake and weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pie warm, often topped with whipped cream, vanilla ice cream, or a drizzle of caramel. It works as a dessert after a meal or as a snack. A cooled slice is convenient for on‑the‑go consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep apple pie in the refrigerator, covered with plastic wrap or in an airtight container, for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a sealed bag for up to 2 months; reheat in the oven before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: A turkey sandwich or sub is a sandwich that uses roasted or smoked turkey as the main filling, often combined with lettuce, tomato, cheese, avocado, and various sauces. It is served on a long roll or baguette and is popular in fast‑food restaurants and cafés.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is considered a leaner meat compared with chicken and beef.
Sub sandwiches got their name from “submarine” because the rolls resemble a submarine’s shape.
In the United States, turkey subs are frequently served with cranberry sauce or mustard.
Turkey was domesticated in Mexico over 2,000 years ago and is now exported worldwide.
Some eateries add bacon strips to the sandwich for extra flavor.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Turkey provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other meats, turkey has a low amount of saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey contains vitamins B3, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Turkey supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Selenium in turkey contributes to antioxidant protection and immune system strength.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked turkey may harbor salmonella; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sandwiches often contain salty sauces and processed meat, raising sodium levels.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to bird meat, which can cause skin reactions or breathing difficulties.

items.title: High calories with add‑ons
items.content: Cheese, sauces, and bacon can significantly increase calories and fat content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turkey sandwiches are usually cut in half and eaten by hand. They can be topped with fresh vegetables, avocado, mustard, mayo, or hummus. For a lighter option, choose a whole‑grain roll and a low‑fat sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A prepared sandwich can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Keep the turkey and sliced veggies separate from the roll to prevent sogginess.

content.title: About
content.content: Raw watermelon is a juicy fruit of the plant Citrullus lanatus, native to Africa. It contains over 90 % water, has a sweet taste and a distinctive aroma. The fruit is usually eaten fresh, but it is also used in juices, smoothies and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Watermelon is one of the oldest cultivated plants, domesticated more than 5,000 years ago in North Africa.
There are over 1,200 varieties of watermelon, differing in flesh color (red, yellow, orange) and shape.
Watermelon seeds are rich in healthy fats and can be dried and eaten as a snack.
Watermelon provides more than 600 ml of water per 100 g, making it an excellent way to stay hydrated in hot weather.
In many cultures watermelon is a symbol of hospitality and celebration.

items.title: High water content
items.content: Helps maintain the body’s fluid balance, especially in heat and during physical activity.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Vitamins B and C
items.content: Support the immune system, collagen synthesis and skin health.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Aids in regulating blood pressure and supporting heart function.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Approximately 30 kcal per 100 g, making watermelon suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to watermelon, such as itching, swelling or hives.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Watermelon has a high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: The rind can carry pesticide residues; it is advisable to wash the fruit thoroughly before eating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Watermelon is typically eaten fresh, cut into wedges or cubes. It can be added to fruit salads, smoothies, cool drinks and refreshing beverages. Dried seeds, when roasted, also make a tasty snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: An uncut watermelon can be kept at room temperature for up to 1 week, or in a cool place for up to 2 weeks. Once cut, cover it with plastic wrap and store in the refrigerator for no more than 3–4 days.

content.title: About
content.content: The yogurt tube is a single‑serve fermented milk product packed in a convenient plastic tube. It has a creamy texture, mild tanginess, and is often flavored with fruit or berry extracts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tube design lets you eat a portion without utensils.
Thanks to airtight packaging, pasteurised yogurt stays fresh up to 30 days without refrigeration.
Yogurt tubes became popular in Russia in the early 2000s as a quick snack for kids and athletes.
Some brands enrich the product with probiotic strains for added gut health benefits.
They are a common item in school lunches because they fit easily into backpacks.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Yogurt provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of probiotics
items.content: Live cultures such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium support intestinal microbiota.

items.title: Low‑fat options
items.content: Reduced‑fat yogurt delivers protein without excess calories.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yogurt supplies vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Lactose is partially broken down by the fermentation process, making it easier to digest.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to yogurt.

items.title: Added sugar in flavored versions
items.content: Fruit‑flavored tubes often contain extra sugar, which can be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Once opened, keep the tube refrigerated and consume within 2–3 days.

items.title: Probiotics and immunocompromised individuals
items.content: Those with weakened immune systems should choose yogurt without live cultures.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The yogurt tube is eaten straight from the package. It can be added to smoothies, used as a topping for fruit, oatmeal or granola, or as a filling for pancakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened tubes in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep the tube refrigerated at 2 °C–6 °C and consume within a few days.
